package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of the struts2-core package contain a critical vulnerability (CVE-2017-5638) that allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server by sending specially crafted HTTP requests with a malicious Content-Type header. This enables remote code execution (RCE) and has been widely exploited in the wild, leading to major data breaches.

execution_context.trigger: HTTP request processing (runtime, upon file upload or form submission)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when processing a multipart/form-data HTTP request, the code parses the Content-Type header and, if invalid, passes it to error handling logic that unsafely evaluates the header value, enabling attacker-supplied code to be executed on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code path allows user-controlled HTTP headers to be interpreted in a way that leads to code execution, which is a classic remote code execution (RCE) vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would be to treat HTTP headers as data, never as executable code. Here, the Content-Type header is unsafely evaluated, violating this expectation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate error handling might log or display header values, but never execute or evaluate them.
key_indicators: User-supplied Content-Type header is parsed and evaluated
Error handling path leads to code execution
No input sanitization or validation on Content-Type

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts an HTTP request with a malicious Content-Type header containing code payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious Content-Type header is processed by the vulnerable Struts2 component.

attack_chain.action: Struts2 error handling logic parses and evaluates the malicious Content-Type header.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution on the server with the privileges of the web server process.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains remote code execution, enabling data exfiltration, privilege escalation, or further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data breach, system compromise, or lateral movement.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected process execution triggered by HTTP requests with unusual Content-Type headers
Multipart/form-data requests resulting in server-side exceptions or command execution
Error handling code paths that parse or evaluate HTTP header values
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with malformed or suspicious Content-Type headers
Outbound connections initiated by the web server process following such requests
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor web server logs for multipart/form-data requests with unusual or malformed Content-Type headers, especially those resulting in errors or exceptions. Detect unexpected process execution or outbound network activity originating from the web server process. Review application code for unsafe parsing or evaluation of HTTP header values, particularly in error handling paths.
